title: claimcheck: Measuring and Improving Specification Faithfulness
abstract: arXiv:2610.17358v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Formal verification proves that a program satisfies its specification, but says nothing about whether the specification captures what the author meant. As LLMs increasingly write both code and specifications, a gap between the author's natural-language requirement and the specification becomes a live risk. A machine-checked proof of a property narrower than the one requested is worthless but passes every check. Closing this gap is solving the spec formalization problem: given a natural-language requirement, produce a formal artifact whose meaning matches it. To measure the gap, we curate an end-to-end benchmark for spec formalization spanning four formal languages: Dafny contracts and Lean 4, Isabelle and Rocq theorem statements. Each of its 3,234 rows pairs a natural-language requirement with a formal artifact and a label established by execution, by proof, or by the benchmark it is drawn from. translated_title: claimcheck：度量与提升规约的忠实性
translated_abstract: 形式化验证能够证明程序满足其规约，却无法说明该规约是否真正捕捉了作者的意图。随着大语言模型越来越多地同时编写代码和规约，作者的自然语言需求与规约之间的差距成为一种现实风险。对被证明的性质窄于所要求性质的机器检查证明毫无价值，却能通过所有检查。弥合这一差距就是解决规约形式化问题：给定一个自然语言需求，生成一个含义与之匹配的形式化工件。为了度量这一差距，我们构建了一个端到端的规约形式化基准，涵盖四种形式语言：Dafny契约以及Lean 4、Isabelle和Rocq的定理陈述。该基准共有3,234条数据，每条数据都将一个自然语言需求与一个形式化工件配对，并带有通过执行、证明或其所来源的基准而确立的标签。其中三分之一的行是保持含义的……
tldr: 该论文提出了claimcheck，一个包含3,234个样本、覆盖Dafny、Lean 4、Isabelle和Rocq四种形式语言的规约形式化基准，用于度量并改进自然语言需求与形式化规约之间的忠实性差距。
